name: NRAS proto-oncogene, GTPase

function.text: NRAS encodes a small GTPase that relays growth-factor signals to pathways including RAF–MEK–ERK and PI3K signaling through regulated GDP/GTP cycling.

germline.text: Strong or definitive GenCC assertions link constitutional variants to Noonan syndrome (autosomal dominant); Noonan syndrome 6 (autosomal dominant).

somatic.text: Somatic alterations are described across multiple tumor groups, including Thymoma; Mucosal melanoma; Cutaneous melanoma. The alteration class and exact variant must be assessed in the disease context.

germline_associations.mechanism: Autosomal dominant; definitive GenCC assertion from ClinGen. Allele-specific mechanism requires review.

function.text: NRAS encodes a small GTPase whose activity is controlled by proteins that promote nucleotide exchange or stimulate GTP hydrolysis. NRAS also cycles between the Golgi apparatus and the plasma membrane. Reversible palmitoylation, regulated by the ZDHHC9-GOLGA7 complex, helps control this trafficking. Regulation of both nucleotide binding and cellular location therefore contributes to the normal control of NRAS signaling.

germline.text: Pathogenic germline variants are associated with Noonan syndrome (autosomal dominant); Noonan syndrome 6 (autosomal dominant).

somatic.text: Somatic alterations involving NRAS have been reported in mucosal melanoma, cutaneous melanoma, and conjunctival melanoma.
